title: Shed litter lands in the canopy, not on the floor
question: Is litter sitting in the crown wrong, or is it the canopy larder that would give ants a reason to climb?
context_md:
**Measured on `main`, 8 trees, 10,800 frames (noon).** `plant.rs::shed_to_litter` writes litter *in place* at the leaf's own position and lets the powder fall, so a leaf shed mid-crown lands on the first branch under it.

Magenta = litter resting on a branch. Cyan = litter resting on the ground. Everything else is the world at quarter brightness — litter's palette is browns and so is wood's, so a plain screenshot cannot tell them apart.

**4,330 litter cells standing: 3,825 on branches, 503 on the ground.** Only 410 are within three rows of the terrain surface.

The creature plan treats this as a defect — floor litter is what a foraging ant can reach, and canopy litter costs sweep time and feeds nobody. But you have said you eventually want ants **climbing trees**, and S4's premise that they can't reach the canopy is already false (measured: ants climb 7/9/0/11 cells up a tree against 0/0/0/0 on bare ground). A crown full of food is exactly the motivation a climb needs.

So I want your call before I change where it lands. I have **not** fixed anything yet.

Also relevant either way: litter is barely rotting. 263 cells rotted against 4,593 ever shed — it inherits ash's global decay rate (dry chance 0.002 per 200-frame check, a ~100,000-frame lifetime) against runs of ~10,000. The floor accumulates monotonically rather than reaching equilibrium.
